text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Striking civil servants will start picketing to strengthen their fight for a 100 percent wage increase, union leader Thomas Banda said on Sunday.

- Malawi President Bakili Muluzi, who is also minister in charge of the civil service, said at the weekend government has no money to award a 100 percent wage increase to public workers as recommended by an independent commission.
- Thirteen other unions have pledged to join striking civil servants in solidarity should the government ignore an ultimatum to increase wages by 100 percent.

- Electricity Supply Commission workers have threatened to launch a national indefinite black-out if the government sacks the commission's Chief Executive Raynolds Duncan, as implied by Energy and Mining Minister Dumbo Lemani's in parliament.
- President Muluzi is likely to drop some ministers from his 36-member cabinet if recommendations by a team of consultants on reform be accepted by government.
- The Customs Workers Union (CWU) could join a civil servant's strike if government continued issuing threats, CWU Secretary General Spencer Phiri said at the weekend.
